question.problem:
$$
V=[\begin{aligned}\,∗\, & -\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \,∗\, & \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $V$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ which of the following could be the first column of the matrix $V?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that since $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of a $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ the matrix $V$ must be a $2\times 2$ orthogonal matrix. This means that 

- the first column must be orthogonal to the second column, and

- the norm of the first column must be equal to $1.$

Among the given options, only the vector $[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]$ has both properties.
